newsitem.title: FRANCE: French rail bill passes Senate despite strike call.
newsitem.headline: French rail bill passes Senate despite strike call.

text.p: A French rail reform bill which has sparked a January 30 strike call by the CGT, CFDT and SUD-Rail trade unions was adopted in the Senate on Friday and goes to the National Assembly on February 4.

The Senate adopted the bill with 223 votes in favour and 94 against, with the opposition Socialists and Communists opposing the bill to create a new state company which would own the network and assume a large chunk of SNCF debts.

The Communist-led CGT and Socialist CFDT, which represent a majority of 180,000 SNCF staff, are calling the one-day strike to protest against a split which they say could open the way to end the SNCF monopoly under European Union deregulation pressure.

The bill would spin 134.2 billion francs ($24 billion) of SNCF debt of 208 billion francs into a new state holding company likely to be called France Rail which would be in charge of investment in the rail network and charge SNCF fees for its use.
The small SUD-Rail union has joined the January 30 strike call after an ineffective strike of its own on Tuesday.
The other minority unions back the bill, which is being put to parliament under an urgent procedure to speed adoption.

Once it gets through the National Assembly -- the lower house -- it will go through a joint Senate-Assembly committee before going for final approval by the two houses of parliament. ($1=5.526 French Franc)
